Endpoint: GET /api/reporting/reports/work-in-progress/export

    &from=2026-01-01T00:00:00.000Z&to=2026-08-04T23:59:59.000Z
    &tab=Completed&columns=wo_number&locations=b3c8c820-f815-4cf1-8938-10956c5ee71a
-> HTTP 500, 173 bytes
   {"errors":[{"error":"An error occurred. We're sorry for this inconvenience, please try again a bit later later."},
              {"requestId":"..."}]}

Request ids captured (all HTTP 500):

  • 709b3abd-de84-41a7-84e8-dc439e7ab76b — format=csv, tab=Completed, default columns
  • c8b1a131-6e1f-462e-b5d6-c69fc87c5663 — format=csv, tab=Completed, columns=wo_number
  • 0a077201-ada0-4048-8d9b-242f9ca5e083 — format=csv, tab=Estimates
  • 31ce90be-3b1a-489f-a3a4-7577db6d4777 — format=csv, tab=ApprovedNotStarted
  • 1eb5693a-fae6-4402-ac47-34c561ec1ff2 — format=pdf, tab=Completed
  • 9c0f272b-e0a8-4e93-99a1-d7e9d4ef5ae9 — format=csv, tab=Completed, no locations parameter

  • columns=zzz -> HTTP 400 Invalid column "zzz".
  • columns omitted -> HTTP 400 At least one column is required.
  • tab omitted -> HTTP 400 Invalid tab "".
  • tab=ApprovedPartiallyCompleted with an empty range -> HTTP 200, 109 bytes, body is the UTF-8 byte-order mark then "Date Range: Jul 31, 2026 - Aug 5, 2026" and "Locations: Staging Heavy Duty - 9919" with no header row and no data rows.

Scope: the same call shape succeeds on the other five reports on this build — sales-by-customer csv 200 (47,480 bytes) and pdf 200 (268,586 bytes), inventory-value csv 200 (724,149 bytes), parts-velocity csv 200 (1,004,398 bytes), technician-utilization csv 200 (926 bytes), sales-by-representative csv 200 (533 bytes).

Not the same as the known PDF size problem: that one is PDF-only, size-dependent, and on the other five reports. This is Work In Progress only, both formats, and it fails with a single row.

"WO #",Status,Customer,Unit,Advisor,"Days Open",Earned,Remaining,Total
S2-15856,Complete,"Gicastle Ventures","OPEN TOP BUS","Kimberly Barnes","53 days","$1,459.25",$101.97,"$1,561.22"

That capture is from an earlier build and an earlier data snapshot, so the change of data cannot be completely excluded as a factor — but the request shape is byte-identical and it now fails on every non-empty tab.

The read endpoint that feeds the same view is healthy: GET /api/reporting/reports/work-in-progress?from=...&to=...&locations=...&tab=...&pagination[rowsPerPage]=1000 returns HTTP 200 with all 392 rows across the four tabs. So the data is fine and the failure is in producing the file.

Requirement S9-R2: "Both downloads include only the columns currently shown, in the same left-to-right order as the screen, with Total last." Requirement S9-R4: "Both downloads include a Totals row matching the on-screen Totals row for the tab." And requirement S9-R9 even names the files: "The downloaded files are named “wip-2-report.pdf” and “wip-2-report.csv”."

A specification that says what is inside the file and what the file is called is asking for a file to be produced. There is nothing to satisfy if the request ends in a server error.

renderedFields.description:
1. Description

On the Work In Progress report, the Asset filter does not offer every asset that is on the report. Where two different vehicles happen to share the same unit number, the filter lists only one of them — and it shows that one's vehicle identification number against the shared unit number. The other vehicle is simply not in the list, so typing its vehicle identification number brings up nothing at all.

The filter is meant to let you type either the unit number or the vehicle identification number. For these vehicles the second half of that promise does not work, and a service manager searching for a truck by the number on its windscreen concludes the truck has no open work, when in fact it has.

On today's test data six vehicles are affected across five shared unit numbers. The clearest one belongs to customer Euwood Paving, which has two different trucks both numbered 854.

Why it matters quietly rather than loudly: the filter looks like it is working. You type a unit number, you get a result, and nothing tells you that a second vehicle with that same number exists and has been left out.

2. Branch / Environment

  • Branch tested: https://sv8582.qa.shopview.com
  • API host: https://sv8582api.qa.shopview.com
  • Build marker (page's app-version): v3.5-16cf83f — index.html last modified Wed, 05 Aug 2026 06:40:32 GMT, etag 177c59546701e7810b894492dabc1423
  • Organisation: d55bc308-e61a-438d-b5f1-c7a73c89d49f
  • Locations selected: both — Staging Heavy Duty - 9919 (b3c8c820-f815-4cf1-8938-10956c5ee71a) and Staging Lethbridge - 4310 (f8a8b802-7780-4b16-bf10-343caeb616b2)
  • Signed in as: admin@shopview.com (Administrator, 42 permissions)
  • Date range used: 1 September 2025 to 5 August 2026 (a wide range so all four tabs have rows)
  • Observed: 2026-08-05, about 18:45 UTC

3. Steps to reproduce

No data needs creating — the vehicles below already exist in the test data and are named exactly.

  1. Sign in as a user who can see reports and open Work In Progress.
  2. Set the Location filter to include both Staging Heavy Duty - 9919 and Staging Lethbridge - 4310.
  3. Set a custom date range of 1 September 2025 to 5 August 2026, so all four tabs have work orders in them.
  4. Open the Asset filter and type 854. One option appears: unit 854 shown with vehicle identification number 5SHFE4730MB001604.
  5. Now clear what you typed and type the full vehicle identification number 1HTKTSWK4RH442544. Nothing matches.
  6. Check that this vehicle really is on the report: it is the asset on work orders S8582-15742 (in the Approved - Partially Completed tab) and S8582-11992 (in the Estimates tab), both for customer Euwood Paving. The same customer's other truck, also unit 854 but with vehicle identification number 5SHFE4730MB001604, is on work orders S8582-15743, S8582-12623, S8582-12086 and S8582-11993.
  7. Repeat with any of the other five affected numbers below and the same thing happens.

The exact assets affected, and the shared unit numbers that cause it:

Unit number Vehicle identification number the filter OFFERS Vehicle identification number the filter LEAVES OUT Work orders carrying the left-out vehicle Customer
854 5SHFE4730MB001604 1HTKTSWK4RH442544 S8582-15742, S8582-11992 Euwood Paving
4 1NKDX4TX0CR955991 3HTMMAAP19N045446 S8582-15133 Iowell Works
4 1NKDX4TX0CR955991 54DC4W1C2GS805134 S8582-15668 Auline Consulting
1 5KJJALD1XEPFP2932 54DC4W1B9ES801599 S8582-15544 Auline Consulting
80 1XKWDR9X2WJ949172 5KKPALDV3DPBY2035 S8582-14030 Suman Solutions
B104 (the option shows no vehicle identification number at all) 5100036463 S8582-15391 Kabridge Enterprises

What was ruled out. The two other filters on the same toolbar are complete, so this is specific to the Asset filter and not a general scope problem:

Filter Values the filter offers Distinct values actually on the report Match
Advisor 15 15 exactly equal, both directions
Customer 215 215 exactly equal, both directions
Asset — by unit number 172 172 exactly equal, both directions
Asset — by vehicle identification number 273 279 six missing

So the filter is not limited to the rows currently loaded — that part works correctly, and it works across all four tabs and both locations. The problem is only that the list is built one entry per unit number. Also ruled out: it is not the date range (the same six are missing on a narrower range), and it is not the B104 case alone — that one has the additional oddity that its option carries no vehicle identification number even though the work order does.

4. Expected behaviour

Every asset that appears on the report should be offered in the Asset filter, and typing either identifier should find it. The Work In Progress specification, version 9, requires (S7-R4):

The toolbar has an Asset filter, a searchable type-ahead multi-select listing the assets present across all open jobs in the current scope. Each option shows the unit number and the vehicle identification number, and the user's typed text matches against EITHER the unit number OR the vehicle identification number.

Two vehicles that share a unit number are still two assets present on the report, so both should be listed and both identification numbers should match.

For non-vehicle assets, note that this field holds the unit's serial number rather than a true vehicle identification number — that is expected and is not what this ticket is about.

5. Current behaviour

The Asset filter offers one entry per unit number. Where two vehicles share a unit number only one is listed, the listed entry shows only that one's identification number, and the other vehicle's identification number matches nothing typed into the filter. Six vehicles are affected on the current test data.

6. Images

No screenshot is attached, and the reason is stated rather than implied: this session could not open the application's screens at all. The application front end would not accept the browser session available to this run, and the one route that produces a signed-in browser could not be used because it would have reset a sign-in shared with two other testers working on other branches at the same time. What is written above was read directly from the data the Asset filter is built from, and the full response is saved with our evidence so the six missing vehicles can be confirmed without repeating the work.

7. Technical details for developers

The option list comes from its own endpoint, separate from the row data:

GET /api/reporting/reports/work-in-progress/filters
    ?from=2025-09-01T00:00:00.000Z&to=2026-08-05T23:59:59.000Z
    &locations=b3c8c820-f815-4cf1-8938-10956c5ee71a,f8a8b802-7780-4b16-bf10-343caeb616b2
-> HTTP 200
   {"data":{"advisors":[15 items],"customers":[215 items],"assets":[278 items]}}

Each asset entry has the shape {{

{"value":"854","unit_number":"854","vin":"5SHFE4730MB001604"}

}}, and value falls back to the identification number when there is no unit number (106 of the 278 entries are of that kind). Counting the 172 entries that do have a unit number: no unit number appears twice, which is the defect — the list is keyed by unit number rather than by asset.

Compared against the complete row set fetched as GET /api/reporting/reports/work-in-progress?...&tab=<each of the four>&pagination[rowsPerPage]=1000 — 392 rows in total (Approved - Partially Completed 116, Approved - Not Started 39, Completed 31, Estimates 206):

Dimension From the rows From the filters endpoint rows minus filters filters minus rows
advisor 15 15 0 0
customer 215 215 0 0
unit_number 172 172 0 0
vin 279 273 6 0

The six: 1HTKTSWK4RH442544, 3HTMMAAP19N045446, 54DC4W1B9ES801599, 54DC4W1C2GS805134, 5100036463, 5KKPALDV3DPBY2035.

Five unit numbers carry more than one identification number across the report: 854 (2), 4 (3), 1 (2), 80 (2), and B104 (a row with 5100036463 and a row with none, while the filter entry has none).

A re-runnable check is in our evidence as tools/wip_probe.py, and the full response plus the 392 rows are saved as evidence/wip-filter-options.json and evidence/wip-all-392-rows.json.

Specification: Work In Progress, Confluence page 703660034, version 9, Story 7 (S7-R4) — the "across all open jobs in the current scope" wording was added in version 9 on 2026-08-05.

Where this expected behaviour comes from: the Work In Progress report specification, version 9, requirement S7-R4, which says: "The toolbar has an Asset filter, a searchable type-ahead multi-select listing the assets present across all open jobs in the current scope. Each option shows the unit number and the vehicle identification number, and the user's typed text matches against EITHER the unit number OR the vehicle identification number." Two different vehicles that share a unit number are two assets present in scope, so both belong in the list.

renderedFields.description:
1. What happens now

When the Sales By Customer or Sales By Representative report is downloaded as a spreadsheet, the numbers inside it arrive dressed up as text. Money comes out as $1,979.40 with a dollar sign and a comma. Percentages come out as 100.0% with a percent sign. Dates come out as Jul 31 2026.

Because those cells are text and not numbers, a person who opens the file in Excel cannot add them up, sort them, or build a pivot table without cleaning every column first.

2. What should happen instead

Both written descriptions ask for plain numbers so the file can be re-used.

  • Sales By Customer, requirement S14-R9: "The Margin % cell is a plain number to one decimal with no percent sign (for example, 64.7)".
  • Sales By Customer, requirement S14-R10: "Dates export as mm-dd-yyyy - for example, 05-14-2026 - matching the ShopView-wide CSV date format."
  • Sales By Customer, requirement S14-R11: "Currency values export as plain numbers with no dollar sign and no thousands separators."
  • Sales By Representative, requirement S14-R17: "numeric columns are emitted as plain numbers for re-pivoting - no currency symbol, thousands separators, or parentheses".

3. How to see it

  1. Sign in and open Reports > Sales By Customer.
  2. Set the date range to Last Month and select the location Staging Heavy Duty - 9919.
  3. Open the three-dot download menu and choose the summary spreadsheet download.
  4. Open the downloaded file in a text editor or Excel.
  5. Repeat the same steps on Reports > Sales By Representative.

Exact test data this was seen with: customer Beman Systems, invoice S-15826, sales representative Parth Fadadu, location Staging Heavy Duty - 9919, date range Last Month (1 - 31 July 2026). Both the summary and the expanded downloads behave the same way on both reports.

4. What was actually in the file

Sales By Customer, summary download:

{noquote}
"Beman Systems",0.0,"$1,979.40","$1,979.40","$2,459.48","$2,459.48",$207.84,"$4,438.88",95.5%,"$4,646.72"{noquote}

Sales By Customer, expanded download - note the date cell:

{noquote}
,,P-126,"Jul 31 2026",0.0,$0.00,$0.00,$16.26,$16.26,$0.00,$16.26,100.0%,$16.26{noquote}

Sales By Representative, expanded download:

{noquote}
,S-15826,"Jul 31 2026","Beman Systems",Unpaid,0.0,0.0,0.0,"$1,979.40","$1,979.40","$2,459.48","$2,459.48","$4,438.88",100.0%,"$4,438.88"{noquote}

5. What was ruled out

renderedFields.description:
1. What happens now

At the bottom of the Inventory Value report there is a summary row that adds up the whole shelf. Its first cell, in the Part # column, reads Totals.

2. What should happen instead

The written description asks for the singular word. Inventory Value requirement S4-R1: "A totals row is shown at the bottom of the report, with the literal label "Total" in the Part # column's cell."

The plural Totals is the label the downloaded files are meant to use - requirement S10 says the downloads "include a totals row matching the on-screen totals, labeled "Totals"". So the two are meant to differ, and the screen is currently using the download's word.

3. How to see it

  1. Sign in and open Reports > Inventory Value.
  2. Leave the date range on This Month and both locations selected.
  3. Scroll to the bottom of the table and read the first cell of the last row.

Exact test data this was seen with: no seeding needed - the organisation's own stock. Locations Staging Heavy Duty - 9919 and Staging Lethbridge - 4310, date range This Month, 5,657 rows in scope.

4. What was actually seen

The last row reads:

{noquote}
Totals | | | | | 195,247.93 | | | $855,066.82 | 46.7% | $1,832,142.09 | $977,075.27{noquote}

Everything else about the row is correct: the Description, Category and Vendor cells are blank, the Unit Cost and Unit Sell cells are blank, the Total Cost cell is bold and pinned to the right, and the row stays visible at the bottom while the rows scroll. Only the word is wrong.

5. What was ruled out

  • It is not a filter effect. The label reads Totals with no filters, with a category chosen, and with a part search applied.
  • It is not the sort. Sorting by any column leaves the row at the bottom, still reading Totals.
  • It is not the download. The download is separately required to say Totals and does. This is the on-screen row.

6. How often

Every time.

7. Where it was seen

Reports > Inventory Value, on the QA branch, build v3.5-16cf83f, on 6 August 2026.

Where this expected behaviour comes from: the Inventory Value report specification, version 4, requirement S4-R1, which says: "A totals row is shown at the bottom of the report, with the literal label “Total” in the Part # column's cell." The word literal is the specification's own.

renderedFields.description:
1. What happens now

The first time somebody opens the Inventory Value report in a browser, every column is already switched on - including Margin and Total Sell.

2. What should happen instead

Those two columns are meant to start switched off, so the report opens on the narrower default view and the user turns them on if they want them.

  • Inventory Value requirement S3-R12: "On first visit, the visible columns are: Part #, Description, Category, Vendor, Qty on Hand, Unit Cost, Unit Sell, Margin %, and Total Cost." Margin and Total Sell are not in that list.
  • Inventory Value requirement S3-R13: "The Margin and Total Sell columns are hidden by default and can be turned on from the column-selection control."
  • Inventory Value requirement S8-R3: "Margin and Total Sell are off by default, the rest on by default."

3. How to see it

  1. Open a browser window that has never opened this report before (a private window works).
  2. Sign in and open Reports > Inventory Value.
  3. Read the column headers across the top of the table.

Exact test data this was seen with: no seeding needed. Locations Staging Heavy Duty - 9919 and Staging Lethbridge - 4310, date range This Month.

4. What was actually seen

The headers on a genuine first visit read:

{noquote}
Part # | Description | Category | Vendor | Location | Qty | Unit Cost | Unit Sell | Margin | Margin % | Total Sell | Total Cost{noquote}

The saved view the page writes for itself on that first load also lists all of them, Margin and Total Sell included.

5. What was ruled out

  • It is not a leftover setting. This was a brand-new browser session with nothing stored for this report - the saved view did not exist until the page created it, and it was created with both columns on.
  • The control itself works. Turning Margin off hides it and turning it back on restores it in the right place, so this is only about the starting state.
  • It is not the separate Location question. The Location column is a different, still-open point. Margin and Total Sell are described plainly in three places with no disagreement.

6. How often

Every time, on every fresh browser.

7. Where it was seen

Reports > Inventory Value, on the QA branch, build v3.5-16cf83f, on 6 August 2026.

Where this expected behaviour comes from: the Inventory Value report specification, version 4, requirement S3-R12, which lists what is on screen at the start: "On first visit, the visible columns are: Part #, Description, Category, Vendor, Qty on Hand, Unit Cost, Unit Sell, Margin %, and Total Cost." Margin and Total Sell are not in that list.

The same specification, requirement S3-R13, says so directly: "The Margin and Total Sell columns are hidden by default and can be turned on from the column-selection control (Story 8)." And requirement S8-R3 repeats it: "Every other column is available in the control; Margin and Total Sell are off by default, the rest on by default (S3-R12)."

renderedFields.description:
1. What happens now

The Inventory Value report remembers most of what the user set - the date range, the locations, the columns and the sort all come back on the next visit. The one thing it forgets is the Search parts box. Whatever was typed there is gone, and the report comes back showing everything.

2. What should happen instead

Inventory Value requirement S8-R5: "The report remembers, in the user's browser, the selected date range, category selection, vendor selection, part search text, location selection, column selection, and sort, and restores them on the user's next visit."

The part search text is named in that list alongside the settings that do come back.

3. How to see it

  1. Sign in and open Reports > Inventory Value.
  2. Type refrigerant into the Search parts box and wait for the table to narrow.
  3. Also click the Part # header once, so the sort changes too.
  4. Navigate away to another screen, then come back to the report.

Exact test data this was seen with: search term refrigerant, which matches the part R134A "Refrigerant" at both locations. Locations Staging Heavy Duty - 9919 and Staging Lethbridge - 4310, date range This Month.

4. What was actually seen

On returning to the report:

  • the Search parts box was empty;
  • the table was back to the full unfiltered list;
  • but the sort had been remembered - it came back on Part # ascending, exactly as it was left.

The saved view the report keeps in the browser holds the date range, the locations, the sort and the columns. There is no entry in it for the search text at all - it is never written, even while the search is active and filtering the table.

5. What was ruled out

  • The search itself works. Typing in the box sends a request and narrows the table correctly. The problem is only that it is not kept.
  • It is not the sort or the columns. Those are remembered correctly, which shows the remembering mechanism is working - the search text is simply not part of what it stores.
  • It is not a timing problem. The search had been applied and the table had already narrowed before navigating away.

6. How often

Every time.

7. Where it was seen

Reports > Inventory Value, on the QA branch, build v3.5-16cf83f, on 6 August 2026.

Where this expected behaviour comes from: the Inventory Value report specification, version 4, requirement S8-R5, which says: "The report remembers, in the user's browser, the selected date range, category selection, vendor selection, part search text, location selection, column selection, and sort, and restores them on the user's next visit." The part search text is named in that list.

renderedFields.description:
1. What happens now

The Inventory Value report remembers the category and vendor a user picked. If one of those saved choices later stops existing in the data, the report keeps using it anyway. The result is a report that opens showing nothing, with no explanation, and no obvious way for the user to work out why - the filter that is emptying the report is one they cannot see any more.

2. What should happen instead

Inventory Value requirement S8-R6: "Restore is defensive: a saved value that is no longer valid falls back to that setting's default rather than breaking the view. A saved category or vendor no longer present in the data is dropped."

So the stale choice should be quietly discarded on load and the report should open on its normal full list.

3. How to see it

  1. Sign in and open Reports > Inventory Value.
  2. Choose a category in the Category filter, so the choice is saved.
  3. Make that saved choice no longer valid - the quickest reliable way is to change the stored category to one that does not exist in the data.
  4. Reload the report.

Exact test data this was seen with: the saved category was replaced with the identifier 00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000000, which matches no category in this organisation. Locations Staging Heavy Duty - 9919 and Staging Lethbridge - 4310, date range This Month, 5,657 rows in scope before the change.

4. What was actually seen

The report loaded without an error message, but:

  • the stale category was not dropped - it was still there in the saved settings afterwards, unchanged;
  • it was still being applied, so the table came back with no data rows at all, down from 5,657.

The user is left looking at an empty report caused by a filter selection that no longer corresponds to anything.

5. What was ruled out

  • It is not a crash. The page renders and no error is shown - which is part of the problem, because nothing tells the user what happened.
  • It is not the rest of the restoring. The date range, locations, columns and sort were all restored correctly in the same load, so the restore path itself is running.
  • It is not a stale-cache effect. The saved settings were re-read after the load and the invalid identifier was still present.

6. How often

Every time.

7. Where it was seen

Reports > Inventory Value, on the QA branch, build v3.5-16cf83f, on 6 August 2026.

Where this expected behaviour comes from: the Inventory Value report specification, version 4, requirement S8-R6, which says: "Restore is defensive: a saved value that is no longer valid falls back to that setting's default rather than breaking the view. A saved category or vendor no longer present in the data is dropped."

renderedFields.description:
1. What happens now

When nothing matches on the Inventory Value report, the user is shown a table with column headings and nothing underneath - no rows, and no message of any kind. There is nothing on the screen to tell them the report ran and found nothing, so it is impossible to tell "no results" apart from "still loading" or "something broke".

2. What should happen instead

The report is meant to show the standard reports no-data message in the data area.

The Inventory Value description says so in three places and spells the words out:

  • Requirement S1-N2: "If no in-stock part exists for the selected location(s) on the resolved date, the report shows the no-data message (Story 12) instead of rows."
  • Requirement S5-N1 and S7-N2 say the same for an out-of-range date and for a location with no stock.
  • The message table at the end of the description gives the exact words: "Empty bays, endless possibilities. Get Going!" - "The application's standard reports no-data label, shown in the data area; the totals row is hidden."

3. How to see it

  1. Sign in and open Reports > Inventory Value.
  2. Type ZZZZNOMATCHZZZZ into the Search parts box.
  3. Wait for the table to reload and look at the data area.

Exact test data this was seen with: search term ZZZZNOMATCHZZZZ, which matches no part. Locations Staging Heavy Duty - 9919 and Staging Lethbridge - 4310, date range This Month, 5,657 rows in scope before the search.

The same empty result can be reached two other ways, and both look the same: choose a date range entirely before nightly recording began (a range in January 2024 returns nothing), or combine two categories with a search term that none of their parts match.

4. What was actually seen

The table contained only its heading row:

{noquote}
Part # | Description | Category | Vendor | Location | Qty | Unit Cost | Unit Sell | Margin | Margin % | Total Sell | Total Cost{noquote}

The words "Empty bays" appear nowhere on the page. The totals row is correctly hidden - that half is right.

5. What was ruled out

  • It is not a loading state. The reload had finished and the server had returned its answer.
  • It is not one route to empty. A no-match search, an out-of-range date and a filter combination that matches nothing all behave the same way.
  • It is not the totals row. Hiding that is correct and it is hidden.

6. How often

Every time, by all three routes.

7. Where it was seen

Reports > Inventory Value, on the QA branch, build v3.5-16cf83f, on 6 August 2026.

Where this expected behaviour comes from: the Inventory Value report specification, version 4, which says three separate times that an empty result shows a message rather than a bare empty table.

Requirement S1-N2: "If no in-stock part exists for the selected location(s) on the resolved date, the report shows the no-data message (Story 12) instead of rows."

Requirement S5-N1: "If there is no recorded day on or before the end of the selected range... the report shows the no-data message (Story 12) and no totals row."

Requirement S7-N2: "If the selected location(s) hold no in-stock parts on the resolved date, the report shows the no-data message (Story 12)."

renderedFields.description:
1. What happens now

The first time somebody opens the Inventory Value report, the Location filter is already set to All locations - every location they can reach - rather than the one location they are currently working at.

For a user at a single branch this means the report opens showing other branches' stock mixed in with their own, and every number in the totals row covers the whole company rather than their shop.

2. What should happen instead

The report should open on the location the user is currently working at, and let them widen it from there.

  • Inventory Value requirement S1-R3: "On the user's first visit (no saved settings), the report defaults to the current calendar month date range and the user's currently active location."
  • Inventory Value requirement S7-R2: "On a first visit (no saved selection), it defaults to the user's currently active location."

The date-range half of S1-R3 is correct - it does open on This Month. It is only the location that is wrong.

3. How to see it

  1. Open a browser window that has never opened this report before (a private window works).
  2. Sign in. Note which location is shown in the top bar - that is the active location.
  3. Open Reports > Inventory Value.
  4. Read the Location filter in the toolbar.

Exact test data this was seen with: the signed-in user's active location was Staging Heavy Duty - 9919, and the account can also reach Staging Lethbridge - 4310.

4. What was actually seen

The Location filter read All locations, and the settings the page saved for itself on that first load listed both location identifiers, not just the active one. Rows from both locations were present in the table and the totals covered both.

5. What was ruled out

  • It is not a leftover setting. This was a brand-new browser session with nothing stored for this report - the saved settings did not exist until the page created them, and it created them with both locations.
  • It is not the filter being broken. Changing the selection works correctly: unticking one location reloads the report scoped to the other.
  • It is not the date range. That part of the same requirement is correct.

6. How often

Every time, on every fresh browser.

7. Where it was seen

Reports > Inventory Value, on the QA branch, build v3.5-16cf83f, on 6 August 2026.

Where this expected behaviour comes from: the Inventory Value report specification, version 4, requirement S1-R3, which says: "On the user's first visit (no saved settings — Story 8), the report defaults to the current calendar month date range and the user's currently active location."

The same specification, requirement S7-R2, repeats it for the filter itself: "On a first visit (no saved selection — Story 8), it defaults to the user's currently active location."

renderedFields.description:
1. What happens now

Two things on the Inventory Value report that the written description asks for are not there.

One. Long text in the Description, Category and Vendor columns is never shortened. The column just keeps growing to fit the longest value and the whole table scrolls sideways instead, so on a narrow screen the user has to scroll a long way right to reach the numbers.

Two. Somebody using a screen reader cannot tell which column the report is sorted by, or in which direction. The arrow is drawn on screen, but nothing is announced.

2. What should happen instead

  • Inventory Value requirement S12-R7: "Long text values (Description, Category, Vendor) are truncated with an ellipsis when they overflow their column, with the full value available on hover; the Part # is never truncated."
  • Inventory Value requirement S12-R8: "Each sortable column header exposes its sort state to assistive technology, and the active sort direction is indicated visually."

The visual half of S12-R8 is correct - the arrow is drawn and the active header is styled. It is only the announced half that is missing.

3. How to see it

The long text:

  1. Sign in and open Reports > Inventory Value.
  2. Make the browser window narrow, about 760 pixels wide.
  3. Find a row with a long description and look at the end of the text, then hover over it.

The sort state:

  1. On the same report, click the Total Cost heading to sort by it.
  2. With an accessibility inspector or a screen reader, read what that heading announces.

Exact test data this was seen with: the longest description in view was "SAE 50 SYNTHETIC TRANSMISSION FLUID BULK (122205) (PER LITER)" on part KL-TF4090, at 61 characters. Locations Staging Heavy Duty - 9919 and Staging Lethbridge - 4310, date range This Month.

4. What was actually seen

Long text: the Description cell is set to never wrap, to let text overflow visibly, and to clip rather than add an ellipsis. Measured on that cell, the visible width and the full content width were the same - 447 pixels each - which means the column had simply grown to fit rather than cutting the text off. There is no ellipsis, and the cell carries no hover text of any kind, so the "full value on hover" has nothing to attach to.

Sort state: none of the twelve column headings carries a sort state for assistive technology, whether it is the sorted column or not. They also carry no heading role. Only the visual arrow and styling change.

5. What was ruled out

  • It is not the window size. The behaviour is the same at 760, 900 and 1680 pixels wide - the column always grows to fit rather than truncating.
  • It is not one column. Description, Category and Vendor all behave the same way.
  • The sorting itself works. Clicking a heading re-sorts correctly and the arrow updates. Only the announcement is missing.

6. How often

Every time.

7. Where it was seen

Reports > Inventory Value, on the QA branch, build v3.5-16cf83f, on 6 August 2026.

Where this expected behaviour comes from: the Inventory Value report specification, version 4, requirement S12-R6, which covers the long text: "Long text values (Description, Category, Vendor) are truncated with an ellipsis when they overflow their column, with the full value available on hover; the Part # is never truncated."

And requirement S12-R8, which covers the headings: "Each sortable column header exposes its sort state to assistive technology, and the active sort direction is indicated visually."

renderedFields.description:
1. What happens now

When the Parts Velocity report is downloaded as a PDF, the long text columns are printed in full instead of being shortened. A description that runs to over a hundred characters is printed complete and simply wraps onto several lines inside its cell, which makes the rows very tall and the page hard to read.

2. What should happen instead

The written description asks for those three columns to be shortened in the PDF.

Parts Velocity specification, version 5, requirement S6-R6: "The PDF is formatted for A3 landscape, titled Parts Velocity. In the PDF, Description, Category, and Vendor are truncated to 18 characters. Part # is not truncated. The CSV carries the full, untruncated Description / Category / Vendor values."

3. How to see it

  1. Sign in as a user who can see reports and open Reports > Parts Velocity.
  2. In the report's own search box type 179.YK5005.
  3. Open the three-dot menu at the top of the report and choose Download (PDF).
  4. Open the downloaded file and look at the Description and Category columns.

Exact test data this was seen with: part number 179.YK5005, description CLEVIS KIT MERITOR TYPE 5/8"Straight, 5/8in-18 Threads, 1/2in and 1/4in Pins, Pin C to C is 1-3/8in(E11430A, R810019) (117 characters), category HD-Air Brakes & Air Suspension (30 characters), vendor Iview Commercial, locations Staging Heavy Duty - 9919 and Staging Lethbridge - 4310, date range This Year.

4. What was actually in the file

The PDF row printed the whole description and the whole category:

{noquote}
Inventory 179.YK5005 CLEVIS KIT MERITOR TYPE 5/8"Straight, 5/8in-18 Threads, 1/2in and 1/4in Pins, Pin C to C is 1-3/8in(E11430A, R810019) HD-Air Brakes & Air Suspension Iview Commercial Staging Lethbridge - 4310 7.00 $5.18 $11.26 $78.82 $42.56 54.0% 8 72 days 43.00{noquote}

Shortened to eighteen characters the description would have read CLEVIS KIT MERITOR and the category HD-Air Brakes & Ai.

5. What was ruled out

  • It is not a reading problem in the file. A second, much shorter part was downloaded the same way and its description, Brake & Parts Cleaner (21 characters), was also printed in full - so nothing at all is being shortened, not just the very long one.
  • It is not the spreadsheet. The spreadsheet is supposed to carry the full text and it does. Only the PDF is wrong.
  • It is not the Part # column. Part # is correctly left alone, which is what the written description asks for.
  • It is not the page size. The PDF is correctly A3 landscape and correctly titled Parts Velocity, and the shop logo is printed.

6. How often

Every time. Three PDF downloads out of three, on three different searches.

7. Where it was seen

Reports > Parts Velocity, on the QA branch, build v3.5-16cf83f, on 6 August 2026.

Where this expected behaviour comes from: the Parts Velocity report specification, version 5, requirement S6-R6, which says: "The PDF is formatted for A3 landscape, titled Parts Velocity. In the PDF, Description, Category, and Vendor are truncated to 18 characters. Part # is not truncated. The CSV carries the full, untruncated Description / Category / Vendor values."

renderedFields.description:
1. What happens now

The Parts Velocity spreadsheet download prints the "Last Sale" column as a piece of text such as 54 days instead of the plain number 54.

Because the cell is text and not a number, somebody who opens the file in Excel cannot sort by it or use it in a calculation without cleaning the column first.

2. What should happen instead

The written description asks for the wording only in the PDF, and a plain number in the spreadsheet.

Parts Velocity specification, version 5, requirement S6-R8: "Last Sale renders as N days (e.g. 42 days) in the PDF; the CSV renders the raw integer."

3. How to see it

  1. Sign in as a user who can see reports and open Reports > Parts Velocity.
  2. In the report's own search box type BRAKECLEAN.
  3. Open the three-dot menu at the top of the report and choose Download (CSV).
  4. Open the downloaded file and look at the Last Sale column.

Exact test data this was seen with: part number BRAKECLEAN, description Brake & Parts Cleaner, locations Staging Heavy Duty - 9919 and Staging Lethbridge - 4310, date range This Year. The file is named velocity-report.csv.

4. What was actually in the file

{noquote}
Inventory,BRAKECLEAN,"Brake & Parts Cleaner",HD-Fluids,—,"Staging Heavy Duty - 9919",512.00,$4.79,$7.69,"$4,332.11","$1,634.06",37.7%,416,"54 days",618.00{noquote}

The cell reads "54 days" where it should read 54.

5. What was ruled out

  • It is not the PDF. The PDF correctly prints 54 days, which is what the written description asks the PDF to do. Only the spreadsheet is wrong.
  • It is not one part. Every row in the file carries the same wording.
  • It is not an empty value. A part with no sale at all correctly prints an em dash in both files, so the empty case is handled properly.

6. How often

Every time. Four spreadsheet downloads out of four.

7. Where it was seen

Reports > Parts Velocity, on the QA branch, build v3.5-16cf83f, on 6 August 2026.

Where this expected behaviour comes from: the Parts Velocity report specification, version 5, requirement S6-R8, which says: "Last Sale renders as N days (e.g. 42 days) in the PDF; the CSV renders the raw integer." So the words belong in the printable file and a plain number belongs in the spreadsheet.

renderedFields.description:
1. What happens now

When a download from the Parts Velocity report finishes, the message that pops up reads "Success - Data exported successfully." That is a general message that could belong to any screen in the application; it does not name the report or say which of the two files was produced.

2. What should happen instead

The written description sets the exact wording, and it names both the report and the file type.

Parts Velocity specification, version 5, requirement S6-R9: "On a successful download, a success toast reads \"Velocity report exported (CSV)\" or \"Velocity report exported (PDF)\"."

3. How to see it

  1. Sign in as a user who can see reports and open Reports > Parts Velocity.
  2. In the report's own search box type BRAKECLEAN, so the view is small enough to download.
  3. Open the three-dot menu at the top of the report and choose Download (CSV). Watch the message that appears.
  4. Do it again and choose Download (PDF). Watch the message that appears.

Exact test data this was seen with: part number BRAKECLEAN, locations Staging Heavy Duty - 9919 and Staging Lethbridge - 4310, date range This Year, type Both.

4. What was actually shown

Both downloads showed the same message:

{noquote}
Success
Data exported successfully.{noquote}

The expected messages were Velocity report exported (CSV) and Velocity report exported (PDF).

5. What was ruled out

  • It is not a missing message. A message does appear, and it appears for both file types - it is the wording that is wrong.
  • It is not the failure message. The failure message is correct: when a download is refused, the message the server sends is passed through and shown to the user word for word, which is what the written description asks for.
  • It is not one file type. The spreadsheet and the PDF both show the same general wording.
  • It is not a timing problem. The message was captured as it appeared, on four separate downloads.

6. How often

Every time. Four downloads out of four.

7. Where it was seen

Reports > Parts Velocity, on the QA branch, build v3.5-16cf83f, on 6 August 2026.

Where this expected behaviour comes from: the Parts Velocity report specification, version 5, requirement S6-R9, which says: "On a successful download, a success toast reads “Velocity report exported (CSV)” or “Velocity report exported (PDF)”." The wording names the report and the file type, which the general message does not.

renderedFields.description:
1. What happens now

Three of the new reports print a heading line in their PDF describing the date range the file covers, and that line always shows an end date one day later than the one that was asked for. It happens on Parts Velocity, on Technician Utilization and on Sales By Customer. On Parts Velocity and Technician Utilization the line also begins with a stray word - it reads "Start Date Range:" rather than "Date Range:". Sales By Customer gets that part right and only has the wrong date.

The spreadsheet download of exactly the same view prints the correct end date, so the two files disagree with each other about the same report.

2. What should happen instead

The heading should describe the range the report was actually run for - if you ask for a range ending on 6 August, the heading should say 6 August. And the label should read "Date Range:", the way it already does on Sales By Customer.

3. How to see it

On Parts Velocity: sign in as a user who can see reports and open Reports > Parts Velocity. In the report's own search box type BRAKECLEAN, so the view is small enough to download. Open the date picker, build a range from 1 January 2026 to 31 July 2026, and press Apply. Open the three-dot menu and choose Download (PDF), then read the heading line under the report title. Then choose Download (CSV) for the same view and read its first line.

On Technician Utilization: open Reports > Technician Utilization, set the date range to This Year, and choose Summary (PDF) from the three-dot menu. Read the heading line.

On Sales By Customer: open Reports > Sales By Customer, leave the date range on This Month, and choose Download Summary (PDF). Read the heading line.

Exact test data this was seen with: organisation Staging Foothills Group Inc; signed-in user Admin ShopView; locations Staging Heavy Duty - 9919 and Staging Lethbridge - 4310. On Parts Velocity, part number BRAKECLEAN with Type set to Both, and three separate ranges were tried. On Technician Utilization, This Year, which returns 29 technicians. On Sales By Customer, This Month, which runs 1 to 6 August 2026.

4. What was actually in the file

Parts Velocity, three ranges, each read from the PDF heading:

  • Asked for 1 Jan 2026 to 31 Jul 2026 - the heading read "Start Date Range: Jan 1, 2026 - Aug 1, 2026".
  • Asked for 1 Feb 2026 to 28 Feb 2026 - the heading read "Start Date Range: Feb 1, 2026 - Mar 1, 2026".
  • Asked for 1 Jan 2026 to 6 Aug 2026 - the heading read "Start Date Range: Jan 1, 2026 - Aug 7, 2026", while the spreadsheet for the same view read "Date Range: Jan 1, 2026 - Aug 6, 2026".

Technician Utilization, asked for 1 Jan 2026 to 6 Aug 2026 - the heading read "Start Date Range: Jan 1, 2026 - Aug 7, 2026".

Sales By Customer, asked for 1 Aug 2026 to 6 Aug 2026 - the heading read "Date Range: Aug 1, 2026 - Aug 7, 2026". The label is right here; only the end date is a day late.

It is not the calendar month rolling over. It happens in the middle of a month too - 28 February came out as 1 March, and 31 July came out as 1 August.

It is not "today" being printed instead. On 6 August the report was asked for a range ending 31 July and the heading read 1 August, not 6 August.

It is not the spreadsheet. The spreadsheet for the same view printed the correct end date on every report checked, so only the PDF heading is affected.

It is not one report's own code. The same one-day-late end date appears on three different reports, which points at the shared piece that builds the PDF heading.

It is not every report. Work In Progress was checked separately and prints its heading correctly - asked for 1 to 2 January 2020 it printed "Jan 1, 2020 - Jan 2, 2020".

Every time. Three PDF downloads out of three on Parts Velocity, and every download taken on Technician Utilization and Sales By Customer.

Reports > Parts Velocity, Reports > Technician Utilization and Reports > Sales By Customer, on the QA branch, build v3.5-16cf83f, on 6 August 2026.

One honest caveat about the label. None of the three specifications writes down the exact words the heading should begin with, so "Start Date Range:" is not breaking a written rule. What makes it wrong is that the same heading on Sales By Customer reads "Date Range:", so the same line is worded two different ways across reports that are meant to match. If the product owner would rather keep "Start Date Range:", that half of this ticket can simply be dropped - the wrong end date stands on its own.

1. What happens now

On the Parts Velocity report the Location column appears in the middle of the table, in sixth place, after Vendor. The written description asks for it to be the first column of all, before Type.

2. What should happen instead

Parts Velocity specification, version 5, requirement S7-R8: "When shown (S2-R12 / S3-R10), the per-row Location column renders as the leftmost column, before Type, using the suite's standard column treatment so its placement matches the same column on the other reports in the suite."

3. How to see it

  1. Sign in as a user who can see more than one location and open Reports > Parts Velocity.
  2. Leave the Location filter on All locations, so more than one location is in view.
  3. Read the column headings from left to right.
  4. Open the three-dot menu and choose Download (CSV), then read the heading row of the downloaded file.

Exact test data this was seen with: locations Staging Heavy Duty - 9919 and Staging Lethbridge - 4310, date range This Year, type Both, no search. The organisation is Staging Foothills Group Inc.

4. What was actually shown

On screen, left to right:

{noquote}
Type | Part # | Description | Category | Vendor | Location | Units Sold | Unit Cost | Sell Price | Revenue | Margin | Margin % | Demand | Last Sale | On Hand{noquote}

The downloaded spreadsheet puts it in the same sixth place:

{noquote}
Type,"Part #",Description,Category,Vendor,Location,"Units Sold","Unit Cost","Sell Price",Revenue,Margin,"Margin %",Demand,"Last Sale","On Hand"{noquote}

5. What was ruled out

  • It is not the column chooser. The Location column is not one of the twenty entries in the column chooser, so a user cannot have moved or re-enabled it - the report places it there itself.
  • The rest of the column behaviour is correct. The column only appears when more than one location is in view; each stocked row shows its own location's name; and a special-order row that covers several locations correctly shows the word Multiple.
  • It is not only the screen. Both downloads place it in the same wrong position, because they follow the screen.

6. How often

Every time, on every view looked at.

7. Where it was seen

Reports > Parts Velocity, on the QA branch, build v3.5-16cf83f, on 6 August 2026.

Where this expected behaviour comes from: the Parts Velocity report specification, version 5, requirement S7-R8, which says: "When shown (S2-R12 / S3-R10), the per-row Location column renders as the leftmost column, before Type, using the suite's standard column treatment so its placement matches the same column on the other reports in the suite."

The same specification, requirement S2-R12, says when it is shown at all: "When the Location filter (S2-R9) resolves to more than one location in scope, the table shows a per-row Location column identifying each row's location; when a single location is in scope the column is hidden."

1. What happens now

The Parts Velocity report opens with its Location filter set to All locations, so the first thing a user sees is every location they have access to, mixed together. The written description asks it to open on the one location the user is actually working in.

2. What should happen instead

Parts Velocity specification, version 5, requirement S2-R9: "The toolbar provides a Location multi-select filter as the rightmost control in the filter row... On a first visit it defaults to the user's currently active location (the location currently selected in the application's global location switcher)."

3. How to see it

  1. Sign in as a user who has access to more than one location. Check the location shown beside your name at the top right - it reads Staging Heavy Duty - 9919.
  2. Open Reports > Parts Velocity for the first time in this browser.
  3. Read the Location filter at the right-hand end of the filter row, and read the Location column in the table.

Exact test data this was seen with: organisation Staging Foothills Group Inc; the signed-in user's active location Staging Heavy Duty - 9919; the other accessible location Staging Lethbridge - 4310. This was a genuine first visit - the browser had no saved view for this report.

4. What was actually shown

The filter read All locations, and the table returned rows from both locations - for example BRAKECLEAN appeared once for Staging Heavy Duty - 9919 and again for Staging Lethbridge - 4310.

5. What was ruled out

  • It is not a remembered setting from an earlier visit. The browser was brand new and held no saved view for this report; the very first request the page sent carried no location at all, and the second carried both.
  • It is not the filter being broken. Choosing a single location works correctly and narrows the report - it is only the starting value that is wrong.
  • It is not a permissions question. Both locations are ones this user is allowed to see.
  • Note for triage: the same starting behaviour was reported on Inventory Value as SV-8931 Open . This ticket is the Parts Velocity report, which has its own requirement wording.

6. How often

Every time. Seen on every fresh browser session opened during this test.

7. Where it was seen

Reports > Parts Velocity, on the QA branch, build v3.5-16cf83f, on 6 August 2026.

Where this expected behaviour comes from: the Parts Velocity report specification, version 5, requirement S2-R9, which says: "The toolbar provides a Location multi-select filter as the rightmost control in the filter row, listing the locations the signed-in user has access to plus an “All Locations” option. On a first visit it defaults to the user's currently active location (the location currently selected in the application's global location switcher)."

renderedFields.description:
1. What happens now

On the Parts Velocity report, long text in the Description, Category and Vendor columns is never shortened. Instead the column simply grows as wide as the longest value in it, which pushes the table far wider than the window and forces the user to scroll sideways to reach the numbers. There is also no tooltip: resting the pointer on a long value shows nothing, because the full value is already on display.

2. What should happen instead

Parts Velocity specification, version 5, requirement S3-R7 is covered by the test as: long Description, Category and Vendor text is shortened with an ellipsis on screen, and the full value is shown on hover. Part # is never shortened.

3. How to see it

  1. Sign in as a user who can see reports and open Reports > Parts Velocity.
  2. In the report's own search box type 179.YK5005.
  3. Look at the Description cell in the row that comes back, and rest the pointer on it.
  4. Notice the horizontal scrollbar under the table.

Exact test data this was seen with: part number 179.YK5005, description CLEVIS KIT MERITOR TYPE 5/8"Straight, 5/8in-18 Threads, 1/2in and 1/4in Pins, Pin C to C is 1-3/8in(E11430A, R810019) (117 characters), category HD-Air Brakes & Air Suspension (30 characters), locations Staging Heavy Duty - 9919 and Staging Lethbridge - 4310, date range This Year, browser window 1680 pixels wide.

4. What was actually shown

The Description cell was 744 pixels wide and held the whole 117-character value with nothing cut off, and it carried no tooltip text at all. The table itself came out 2,429 pixels wide inside a 1,372 pixel space, so roughly a thousand pixels of it sat off-screen.

5. What was ruled out

  • It is not the window being too narrow. The cell is not clipped at all - it is sized to fit the whole value, so the text is complete and the table is simply too wide.
  • It is not the Part # column. Part # is correctly left alone, which is what the written description asks for.
  • It is not one long value. Category behaves the same way - a 30-character category is shown in full in a 217-pixel cell.
  • Note for triage: the same behaviour was reported on Inventory Value as SV-8932 Open . This ticket is the Parts Velocity report.

6. How often

Every time, on every row looked at.

7. Where it was seen

Reports > Parts Velocity, on the QA branch, build v3.5-16cf83f, on 6 August 2026.

Where this expected behaviour comes from: the Parts Velocity report specification, version 5, requirement S3-R7, which says: "The Description, Category, and Vendor columns truncate long text with an ellipsis on screen; the full value is available on native hover (browser tooltip) and is written in full to the CSV export (S6). Part # is never truncated (on screen or in any export)."

renderedFields.description:
1. What happens now

A technician's Total Hours on Technician Utilization does not agree with the same technician's total on the Timesheet Activities report, even when both cover the same dates, the same single location and only finished clock records. The gap is small but real - up to a quarter of an hour on the technicians checked.

2. What should happen instead

Technician Utilization specification, version 6, requirement S1-R9: "For the same date range and the same single location, and counting closed clock records, this report's Total Hours for a technician equals the Timesheet Activities report's total for that technician to the cent."

The same specification, section 3: "The Timesheet Activities report rounds the same way this report does (round-half-up, two decimals) from the same clock data; the to-the-cent reconciliation (S1-R9) depends on that shared rounding."

3. How to see it

Open Reports > Technician Utilization, set the date range to This Year and choose the single location Staging Heavy Duty - 9919.

Find the row for Andrew Wade and write down his Total Hours.

Click that Total Hours figure. Timesheet Activities opens for the same technician and the same dates. Wait for the page to finish loading - the staff name settles to Andrew Wade - and read the Totals line at the bottom.

Exact test data this was seen with: organisation Staging Foothills Group Inc; signed-in user Admin ShopView; active location Staging Heavy Duty - 9919; the other accessible location Staging Lethbridge - 4310; date range This Year (1 January 2026 to 6 August 2026), which returns 29 technicians. The technicians compared were Andrew Wade, Brittany Anderson, Colleen Guerrero, Fernando Mercer, Kellie Ayers, Angela Roman, Christian Pitts and Alyssa Randall.

4. What was actually shown

Technician Utilization showed Andrew Wade 1080.44 hours. Timesheet Activities showed 1080.64 for the same technician and dates - a difference of 0.20 hours.

Six of the eight technicians compared disagreed: Andrew Wade +0.20, Fernando Mercer +0.25, Kellie Ayers +0.21, Brittany Anderson +0.16, Colleen Guerrero +0.05, Angela Roman -0.01 and Christian Pitts -0.03. Alyssa Randall matched exactly at 744.51.

The likely cause, from the underlying data: Timesheet Activities adds up each clock record after that record has already been rounded to two decimals, while Technician Utilization adds up the raw times and rounds once at the end. Andrew Wade's 604 individual records add up to 1080.62 once each has been rounded, against 1080.4422 raw.

5. What was ruled out

It is not an open clock. Andrew Wade has no clock records at all in August 2026, so nothing was still running when either report was read, and the two readings were taken two seconds apart.

It is not the multi-location drill-through difference the specification allows. Technician Utilization was scoped to the single location Staging Heavy Duty - 9919, which is also the shop the user is signed in to, and this technician has no hours at the other location - his figure is identical whether one location or both are selected.

It is not a date-range difference. Both reports covered 1 January 2026 to 6 August 2026.

Note for triage: two older tickets described a similar disagreement between the previous reports and Timesheet Activities - SV-6431 Done (Done) and SV-5334 OBSOLETE (obsolete). This one is about the new Technician Utilization report.

6. How often

Every time, and on most technicians - six of the eight checked.

7. Where it was seen

Reports > Technician Utilization, on the QA branch, build v3.5-16cf83f, on 6 August 2026.

Where this expected behaviour comes from: the Technician Utilization report specification, version 6, requirement S1-R9, which says: "Reconciliation guarantee (scope). For the same date range and the same single location, and counting closed clock records, this report's Total Hours for a technician equals the Timesheet Activities report's total for that technician to the cent."

renderedFields.description:
1. What happens now

Clicking a column heading on Technician Utilization sends a fresh request to the server and waits for new rows. The written description asks for the rows already on screen to be reordered without any reload.

2. What should happen instead

Technician Utilization specification, version 6, requirement S2-R13: "All six columns... are sortable by clicking the column header... Sorting is applied on screen to the loaded rows (no reload)."

3. How to see it

Open Reports > Technician Utilization and set the date range to This Year so there are plenty of rows.

Click the Total Hours heading once, then again.

Watch the table: it briefly clears and refills each time rather than simply reordering.

Exact test data this was seen with: organisation Staging Foothills Group Inc; signed-in user Admin ShopView; active location Staging Heavy Duty - 9919; the other accessible location Staging Lethbridge - 4310; date range This Year (1 January 2026 to 6 August 2026), which returns 29 technicians.

4. What was actually shown

Each click sent a new request to the report's own data address carrying the sort as part of the request - first with the sort marked not-descending, then with it marked descending. The rows came back from the server rather than being reordered in the page.

5. What was ruled out

It is not the sort being wrong. The order itself is correct: the first click on Technician sorts Z to A, the next A to Z, with no third state, and Est. Lost Labor sorts correctly both ways.

It is not a one-off. It happened on every column tried - Technician, Total Hours and Est. Lost Labor.

It is not the report reloading for another reason. The date range and the location selection were untouched between the clicks.

6. How often

Every time, on every column.

7. Where it was seen

Reports > Technician Utilization, on the QA branch, build v3.5-16cf83f, on 6 August 2026.

Where this expected behaviour comes from: the Technician Utilization report specification, version 6, requirement S2-R13, which says: "All six columns (Technician, Total Hours, WO Hours, Internal Hours, Utilization %, Est. Lost Labor) are sortable by clicking the column header. Clicking a column that is not the active sort sorts it ascending; clicking the active sort column again toggles it to descending."

That the sort happens on screen rather than by asking the server again is stated in requirement S7-R10a: "The on-screen column sort (S2-R13) is applied client-side only and is not carried into the export."

renderedFields.description:
1. What happens now

Ticking or unticking a technician in the Technician Utilization technician filter sends a fresh request to the server. The written description says this filter should work on screen only - hiding and showing rows and recalculating the Summary - unlike the location filter, which does reload.

2. What should happen instead

Technician Utilization specification, version 6, requirement S9-R3: "Selecting one, several, or all locations reloads the report scoped to that set (unlike the technician filter, which is on-screen only)."

The same specification, requirement S4-R5, calls deselecting and re-selecting a technician "an on-screen operation".

3. How to see it

Open Reports > Technician Utilization and set the date range to This Year.

Open the Technician filter and untick one technician - Christian Pitts was used.

Watch the table: it reloads rather than simply hiding the row.

Exact test data this was seen with: organisation Staging Foothills Group Inc; signed-in user Admin ShopView; active location Staging Heavy Duty - 9919; the other accessible location Staging Lethbridge - 4310; date range This Year (1 January 2026 to 6 August 2026), which returns 29 technicians.

4. What was actually shown

Unticking Christian Pitts sent a new request to the report's own data address carrying an exclusion list with that technician in it, and the rows came back from the server. The row count went from 29 to 28 and the Summary recalculated correctly - the outcome is right, it is the reload that is not.

The Summary moved from 15916.03 / 12843.23 / 3072.80 / 80.7% / $462,687.13 to 14984.33 / 12811.99 / 2172.34 / 85.5% / $332,120.67.

5. What was ruled out

It is not the filter being wrong. Hiding, showing and the Summary recalculation are all correct, and the deselected technicians are remembered exactly as described.

It is not the location filter being confused with it. The location selection was unchanged throughout.

It is not the same fault as the sorting reload, which is reported separately - that one happens on a column heading click, this one on a filter change.

6. How often

Every time, on every technician tried.

7. Where it was seen

Reports > Technician Utilization, on the QA branch, build v3.5-16cf83f, on 6 August 2026.

Where this expected behaviour comes from: the Technician Utilization report specification, version 6, requirement S9-R3, which draws the distinction in its own words: "Selecting one, several, or all locations reloads the report scoped to that set (unlike the technician filter, which is on-screen only)."

The same specification, requirement S4-R5, depends on that being true: "Expansion state is view-only and is not persisted: it resets (all collapsed) on any data reload (date-range or location change) and on a fresh visit. Deselecting and re-selecting a technician in the technician filter (an on-screen operation) does not change the expansion state of the other rows."

1. What happens now

The technician filter on Technician Utilization is labelled "Technician", and the control that selects everybody is labelled "All technicians". The written description asks for "Filter by Technician" and "Select all".

2. What should happen instead

Technician Utilization specification, version 6, requirement S5-R1: "The toolbar has a filter labeled 'Filter by Technician' where the user can select more than one technician."

The same specification, requirement S5-R6: "The filter has a control labeled 'Select all' to select all technicians at once."

3. How to see it

Read the label above the technician filter in the toolbar - it reads "Technician".

Open that filter and read the first two entries - they read "All technicians" and "Clear all".

4. What was actually shown

The toolbar label is "Technician". The first entry in the list is "All technicians" where the description asks for "Select all". The second entry, "Clear all", matches.

5. What was ruled out

It is not a translation or a display width problem - the full words are shown and there is room for more.

It is not the control being wrong. Both controls do exactly what they should; only the wording differs.

Note for triage: the download menu on this same report has a related wording difference, already reported as SV-8881 Open .

6. How often

Every time.

7. Where it was seen

Reports > Technician Utilization, on the QA branch, build v3.5-16cf83f, on 6 August 2026.

renderedFields.description:
1. What happens now

Every Technician Utilization download contains all technicians, whatever is ticked in the technician filter. Unticking someone on screen does not remove them from the file, and choosing a download with nobody ticked still produces a full file with a success message.

2. What should happen instead

Technician Utilization specification, version 6, requirement S7-R8: "Every download includes only the technicians that are currently selected in the technician filter, and covers the location(s) currently selected in the location filter."

The same specification, Story 7 note S7-N1, says a download chosen with no technician selected should do nothing at all - no file and no message.

3. How to see it

Open Reports > Technician Utilization and set the date range to This Year.

Open the technician filter and untick one technician - Andrew Wade was used. The toolbar then reads 28 technicians and his row disappears from the table.

Open the three-dot menu and choose Summary (CSV). Open the file and search for Andrew Wade.

Then untick everybody with "Clear all" - the table shows the empty message - and choose Summary (CSV) again.

Exact test data this was seen with: organisation Staging Foothills Group Inc; signed-in user Admin ShopView; active location Staging Heavy Duty - 9919; the other accessible location Staging Lethbridge - 4310; date range This Year (1 January 2026 to 6 August 2026), which returns 29 technicians.

4. What was actually shown

With Andrew Wade unticked, the downloaded spreadsheet still held 29 technician rows including his - 1080.44 hours. The request the page sent for the file carried the dates and the locations but nothing at all about the technician filter.

With every technician unticked, the download still arrived - the same full 29-row file - and a success message appeared reading "Success / Data exported successfully."

5. What was ruled out

It is not the filter failing on screen. The row really does disappear and the Summary really does recalculate; it is only the download that ignores it.

It is not the location or the date range being ignored too. Both are carried into the download correctly, and the file's own heading lines show the right range and locations.

It is not a stale file from an earlier download. Each file was fetched fresh and its contents read.

6. How often

Every time, on both the spreadsheet and the PDF.

7. Where it was seen

Reports > Technician Utilization, on the QA branch, build v3.5-16cf83f, on 6 August 2026.

Where this expected behaviour comes from: the Technician Utilization report specification, version 6, requirement S7-R8, which says: "Every download includes only the technicians that are currently selected in the technician filter, and covers the location(s) currently selected in the location filter."

The same specification, requirement S7-N1, covers the empty case: "If no technician is selected, choosing a download option does nothing: no file downloads and no message appears."

1. What happens now

The rows in a Technician Utilization download are in no recognisable order. The written description asks every download to be ordered by technician name from A to Z.

2. What should happen instead

Technician Utilization specification, version 6, requirement S7-R10a: "Rows in every download are ordered by Technician name A to Z (the default order). The on-screen column sort is applied client-side only and is not carried into the export."

3. How to see it

Open Reports > Technician Utilization and set the date range to This Year.

Open the three-dot menu and choose Summary (CSV), then Summary (PDF).

Read the technician names in order down each file.

Exact test data this was seen with: organisation Staging Foothills Group Inc; signed-in user Admin ShopView; active location Staging Heavy Duty - 9919; the other accessible location Staging Lethbridge - 4310; date range This Year (1 January 2026 to 6 August 2026), which returns 29 technicians.

4. What was actually shown

Both files begin: Alexander Cohen, Brittany Anderson, Colleen Guerrero, Wesley Mcclure, Jacob Chung, William Johns, Judy Garcia, Andrew Wade, Monica Miller, Frank Hendrix - and end with Admin ShopView, Taylor Kelley, Margaret Garcia, Veronica Miller, Christopher Cobb. That is neither alphabetical nor the order on screen.

The on-screen table at the moment of download was sorted correctly by Technician A to Z.

5. What was ruled out

It is not the on-screen sort leaking into the file. The screen was in its default A to Z order when the files were taken, and the files were still unordered; the request for the file carries no sort instruction at all.

It is not a spreadsheet-only problem - the PDF has exactly the same order.

It is not the order the server returns for the table. The table's own request returns the technicians alphabetically.

6. How often

Every time, in both file types.

7. Where it was seen

Reports > Technician Utilization, on the QA branch, build v3.5-16cf83f, on 6 August 2026.

Where this expected behaviour comes from: the Technician Utilization report specification, version 6, requirement S7-R10a, which says: "Rows in every download are ordered by Technician name A→Z (the default order). The on-screen column sort (S2-R13) is applied client-side only and is not carried into the export."

renderedFields.description:
1. What happens now

None of the four Technician Utilization downloads contains the Summary row. The files end on the last technician. The written description asks for the Summary row in every one of them.

2. What should happen instead

Technician Utilization specification, version 6, requirement S7-R5: "The Summary PDF shows the technician rows and the Summary row."

The same specification, requirement S7-R6: "The Expanded PDF shows the technician rows, each technician's per-day breakdown, and the Summary row."

The same specification, requirement S7-R7: "The CSV file shows the technician rows and the Summary row."

3. How to see it

Open Reports > Technician Utilization and set the date range to This Quarter, so there is only one technician and the files are short.

Note the Summary row at the bottom of the table on screen.

Open the three-dot menu and take all four downloads in turn. Look at the last line of each file.

Exact test data this was seen with: organisation Staging Foothills Group Inc; signed-in user Admin ShopView; active location Staging Heavy Duty - 9919; the other accessible location Staging Lethbridge - 4310; date range This Year (1 January 2026 to 6 August 2026), which returns 29 technicians. This Quarter returns the single technician Admin ShopView with 1.31 hours.

4. What was actually shown

Every file ends on the last technician row. The Summary row - which on screen reads "Summary 15916.03 12843.23 3072.80 80.7% $462,687.13" for This Year - is not in any of them.

This was checked on both the short This Quarter view and the full This Year view, in the spreadsheets and in the PDFs.

5. What was ruled out

It is not the row being on a page nobody looked at. The PDF's last page ends on the last technician above the footer, and the spreadsheet's last line is the last technician.

It is not the Summary row being missing on screen - it is present and correct there, and its figures were checked against the underlying data.

It is not a filter side-effect. Nothing was unticked when these files were taken.

6. How often

Every time, in all four downloads.

7. Where it was seen

Reports > Technician Utilization, on the QA branch, build v3.5-16cf83f, on 6 August 2026.

Where this expected behaviour comes from: the Technician Utilization report specification, version 6, which names the Summary row in all three files — requirement S7-R5: "The Summary PDF shows the technician rows and the Summary row."; requirement S7-R6: "The Expanded PDF shows the technician rows, each technician's per-day breakdown, and the Summary row."; requirement S7-R7: "The CSV file shows the technician rows and the Summary row."

fields.summary: Technician Utilization downloads leave out the Summary row

renderedFields.description:
1. What happens now

Technician Utilization offers two spreadsheet downloads and they are not the same. The Expanded one contains a row for every day each technician worked; the written description says the spreadsheet is always the summary-level content whichever option is chosen. The three file names also differ from the ones written down.

2. What should happen instead

Technician Utilization specification, version 6, requirement S7-R7: "The CSV file shows the technician rows and the Summary row. The CSV is always this summary-level content; it does not vary by the summary/expanded choice."

The same specification, requirement S7-R12: "The downloaded files are named 'Technician-Utilization-Summary.pdf', 'Technician-Utilization-Expanded.pdf', and 'technician-utilization.csv'."

3. How to see it

Open Reports > Technician Utilization and set the date range to This Quarter so the files are short.

Open the three-dot menu and choose Summary (CSV), then Expanded (CSV). Also take the two PDFs.

Open both spreadsheets and compare them, and write down the four file names.

Exact test data this was seen with: organisation Staging Foothills Group Inc; signed-in user Admin ShopView; active location Staging Heavy Duty - 9919; the other accessible location Staging Lethbridge - 4310; date range This Year (1 January 2026 to 6 August 2026), which returns 29 technicians. This Quarter returns the single technician Admin ShopView with 1.31 hours on 5 August 2026.

4. What was actually shown

The Summary spreadsheet holds one technician row. The Expanded spreadsheet holds the same technician row plus a per-day row beneath it - "Staging Lethbridge - 4310, 2026-08-05, 1.31, 1.31, 0.00, 100.0%, $0.00".

The four names given were technician-utilization-summary.csv, technician-utilization-expanded.csv, technician-utilization-summary.pdf and technician-utilization-expanded.pdf. The description asks for two Title-Case PDF names and a single lower-case spreadsheet name, technician-utilization.csv.

5. What was ruled out

It is not the expanded view being wrong in itself - a per-day breakdown is exactly what the Expanded PDF is meant to hold, and it does.

It is not a naming clash caused by taking two files in a row. Each was fetched separately and the name came from the download itself.

Note for triage: a second spreadsheet option exists at all because of the product owner's answer of 5 August 2026 (item T2-6, option B). What that answer did not settle is whether the second spreadsheet should hold the per-day rows or the same summary content, and what the two files should be called. That part may be a question for the product owner rather than a fix.

6. How often

Every time.

7. Where it was seen

Reports > Technician Utilization, on the QA branch, build v3.5-16cf83f, on 6 August 2026.

Where this expected behaviour comes from: the Technician Utilization report specification, version 6, requirement S7-R7, which says what the spreadsheet holds: "The CSV file shows the technician rows and the Summary row. The CSV is always this summary-level content; it does not vary by the summary/expanded choice." Per-day rows are not part of that.

The same specification, requirement S7-R12, names the files: "The downloaded files are named “Technician-Utilization-Summary.pdf”, “Technician-Utilization-Expanded.pdf”, and “technician-utilization.csv”."
