renderedFields.description:
1. What happens now

When a Technician Utilization download starts, the message reads "Success / Data exported successfully." When a download fails, no message appears at all - the user is simply left with no file and no explanation.

2. What should happen instead

Technician Utilization specification, version 6, Story 7 error handling and the section 7 notifications table close both wordings: a download that starts shows "Download started", and a download that fails shows "Failed to download report".

3. How to see it

Open Reports > Technician Utilization and set the date range to This Quarter. Open the three-dot menu, choose Summary (CSV), and read the message that appears.

Then set the date range to This Year and choose Expanded (PDF). Wait about forty seconds and watch for any message.

Exact test data this was seen with: organisation Staging Foothills Group Inc; signed-in user Admin ShopView; active location Staging Heavy Duty - 9919; the other accessible location Staging Lethbridge - 4310; date range This Year (1 January 2026 to 6 August 2026), which returns 29 technicians.

4. What was actually shown

The successful download showed "Success / Data exported successfully." - the same generic wording for all four options, naming neither the report nor the file type.

The failed download showed nothing. The server answered the request with an error after roughly half a minute, no file arrived, and no message of any kind was displayed.

5. What was ruled out

It is not a message that appeared and vanished before it could be read. The screen was checked continuously for forty-five seconds after the failure and no notification was ever present.

It is not the download quietly succeeding. No file was produced.

Note for triage: the underlying reason that Expanded PDF fails on a large view is already reported as SV-8818 Ready to Fix , which names this report. This ticket is only about the missing and generic messages.

Note for triage: the same generic success wording was reported on Parts Velocity as SV-8936 Open . This ticket is the Technician Utilization report, which has its own written wordings.

6. How often

Every time, for both the success and the failure message.

7. Where it was seen

Reports > Technician Utilization, on the QA branch, build v3.5-16cf83f, on 6 August 2026.

Where this expected behaviour comes from: the Technician Utilization report specification, version 6, Story 7 under Error Handling, which gives both wordings: "When a download starts, the user sees a success notification: “Download started”." and "If a download fails, the user sees an error notification: “Failed to download report”."

The same two appear again in the notifications table in section 7 of that specification, where the trigger "A download starts" is paired with the message "Download started", and the trigger "A download fails" with the message "Failed to download report".

renderedFields.description:
1. What happens now

The arrow controls that open a technician's daily breakdown, and the one in the table heading that opens them all, do not report whether they are currently open or closed to a screen reader. Their names change, but the open/closed state itself is never exposed.

2. What should happen instead

Technician Utilization specification, version 6, requirement S8-R12: "The expand/collapse controls (per-row S4-R1 and the all-rows control S4-R4) are keyboard-focusable, toggle on Enter/Space, expose their expanded/collapsed state to assistive technology, and carry the verbatim accessible names defined in S4-R1 (per-row) and S4-R4 (all-rows)."

3. How to see it

Open Reports > Technician Utilization and set the date range to This Year.

Put a screen reader on the arrow control at the left of any technician row, then open the row and listen again.

Do the same with the double-arrow control in the table heading.

Exact test data this was seen with: organisation Staging Foothills Group Inc; signed-in user Admin ShopView; active location Staging Heavy Duty - 9919; the other accessible location Staging Lethbridge - 4310; date range This Year (1 January 2026 to 6 August 2026), which returns 29 technicians. The technician used was Christian Pitts.

4. What was actually shown

The names are correct and do change: "Expand Christian Pitts's daily breakdown" when closed and "Collapse Christian Pitts's daily breakdown" when open, and "Expand all technicians" / "Collapse all technicians" on the heading control. But neither control carries the standard expanded/collapsed state, so a screen reader announces the name only and never the state.

5. What was ruled out

It is not the names being wrong - they match the written wording exactly, in both states, for both controls.

It is not the controls being unreachable. Both are ordinary focusable buttons.

It is not limited to one row. Every technician row behaves the same way, and so does the heading control.

6. How often

Every time, on every row.

7. Where it was seen

Reports > Technician Utilization, on the QA branch, build v3.5-16cf83f, on 6 August 2026.

Where this expected behaviour comes from: the Technician Utilization report specification, version 6, requirement S4-R1, which says: "Each technician row has a control to expand and collapse it. The control carries an accessible name reflecting its next action, scoped to that technician (“Expand 's daily breakdown” when the row is collapsed, “Collapse 's daily breakdown” when it is expanded)."

Requirement S4-R4 asks for the same of the all-rows control, and requirement S8-R12 states the accessibility duty outright: "The expand/collapse controls (per-row S4-R1 and the all-rows control S4-R4) are keyboard-focusable, toggle on Enter/Space, expose their expanded/collapsed state to assistive technology, and carry the verbatim accessible names defined in S4-R1 (per-row) and S4-R4 (all-rows)."

renderedFields.description:
1. What happens now

The per-row Location column on Technician Utilization vanishes as soon as the user narrows the location filter to a single location, and there is no way to bring it back - the Location column is not offered in the Column Selection control at all. The written description ties the column to how many locations the user can reach, not to how many are currently chosen, and asks for it to be one of the columns the user can switch on and off.

2. What should happen instead

Technician Utilization specification, version 6, requirement S9-R9: "The report shows a per-row Location column to any user with access to more than one location; it is shown by default and can be toggled on or off from the column selector, and a user with access to only one location never sees it."

The same specification, requirement S10-R4: "The per-row Location column is one of the toggleable columns for a user with access to more than one location: it is shown by default and can be toggled on or off from the column selector."

3. How to see it

Sign in as a user who can reach both locations and open Reports > Technician Utilization. The Location column is there, leftmost, before Technician.

Open the Location filter and choose only Staging Heavy Duty - 9919.

Look at the table again, then open the Column Selection control and look for Location.

Exact test data this was seen with: organisation Staging Foothills Group Inc; signed-in user Admin ShopView; active location Staging Heavy Duty - 9919; the other accessible location Staging Lethbridge - 4310; date range This Year (1 January 2026 to 6 August 2026), which returns 29 technicians.

4. What was actually shown

With one location chosen the headings became Technician, Total Hours, WO Hours, Internal Hours, Utilization %, Est. Lost Labor - the Location column was gone.

The Column Selection control offers only Total Hours, WO Hours, Internal Hours, Utilization % and Est. Lost Labor. Location is not in the list in either state, so it can be neither switched off when it is there nor switched on when it is not.

5. What was ruled out

It is not the user losing access to the second location - both remain available in the filter and can be re-selected, which brings the column straight back.

It is not the column simply being empty. It is absent: there is no such heading and no such cell.

Note for triage: the specification is not perfectly consistent on the first half. renderedFields.description:
1. What happens now

Nothing a user chooses on Sales By Customer ever appears in the browser's address bar. The address stays at the plain report address whatever the date range, whatever the Product Type. So the report cannot be shared or bookmarked at a particular range - the person you send it to just gets their own saved view.

2. What should happen instead

Sales By Customer specification, version 15, requirement S2-R6: "When the user changes the date range, the chosen value is written to the page link so the report can be shared or bookmarked at that range."

The same specification, requirement S3-R7 carries the Product Type into the exports, and requirement S9-R3: "Before navigating, the active date range and Product Type are written to the page link so the report can be restored."

3. How to see it

Open Reports > Sales By Customer and look at the browser address bar.

Change the date range to Last Month and apply it. Watch the address bar for at least fifteen seconds.

Change the Product Type to Service only. Watch the address bar again.

Expand a customer, then an asset, and click an invoice number. Look at the address you came from.

Exact test data this was seen with: organisation Staging Foothills Group Inc; signed-in user Admin ShopView; active location Staging Heavy Duty - 9919; the other accessible location Staging Lethbridge - 4310; Product Type left at Parts & Service unless the step says otherwise.

4. What was actually shown

The address stayed exactly /reports/sales-by-customer at every point - after the date change (sampled ten times over fifteen seconds), after the Product Type change, and at the moment of clicking through to an invoice.

Everything else about those steps works: the report really does reload for the new range and the new Product Type, and coming back with the browser's back button restores Last Month and Service Only correctly and collapses the expanded rows.

5. What was ruled out

It is not a delayed write. The address was sampled ten times at 1.5-second intervals after the range was applied and never changed.

It is not the setting failing to take effect - the request the page sent carried the new range and the new Product Type each time.

It is not the saved view masking it. The saved view is a separate mechanism and it works; this is about the address bar, which stays bare.

6. How often

Every time, for every filter tried.

7. Where it was seen

Reports > Sales By Customer, on the QA branch, build v3.5-16cf83f, on 6 August 2026.

Where this expected behaviour comes from: the Sales By Customer report specification, version 15, requirement S2-R6, which says: "When the user changes the date range, the chosen value is written to the page link so the report can be shared or bookmarked at that range."

The same specification, requirement S9-R3, adds the Product Type: "Before navigating, the active date range and Product Type are written to the page link so the report can be restored."

renderedFields.description:
1. What happens now

A Sales By Customer download is always called the same thing whatever period it covers, so two files taken for different date ranges are indistinguishable once they are saved.

2. What should happen instead

Sales By Customer specification, version 15, requires the file name to carry the period: the Summary file is named sales-by-customer-summary-

{range} and the Expanded file sales-by-customer-expanded-{range}

, where

{range} is the period that was chosen (this_week, last_week, this_month, last_month, this_year, last_year, this_quarter, last_quarter).

3. How to see it

Open Reports > Sales By Customer with the date range on This Month.

Open the three-dot menu, choose Download Summary (CSV), and note the file name.

Choose Download Expanded View (CSV) and note that one too.

Exact test data this was seen with: organisation Staging Foothills Group Inc; signed-in user Admin ShopView; active location Staging Heavy Duty - 9919; the other accessible location Staging Lethbridge - 4310; Product Type left at Parts & Service unless the step says otherwise.

4. What was actually shown

The two files were called sales-by-customer-summary.csv and sales-by-customer-expanded.csv - correct apart from the missing period. There is nothing in either name to say which range it covers.

The files themselves are right: each begins with a "Date Range: Aug 1, 2026 - Aug 6, 2026" line and a "Locations: All locations" line, so the information is in the file, just not in its name.

5. What was ruled out

It is not the browser shortening the name - the name comes from the download itself.

It is not a Summary-only or a spreadsheet-only problem; both spreadsheet options behave the same way.

It is not the range being ignored - the file contents cover exactly the chosen range.

6. How often

Every time.

7. Where it was seen

Reports > Sales By Customer, on the QA branch, build v3.5-16cf83f, on 6 August 2026.



Where this expected behaviour comes from: the Sales By Customer report specification, version 15, requirement S14-R14, which says: "The files are named for the report, the version, and the active date range: the Summary CSV is sales-by-customer-summary-{range}

.csv and the Expanded CSV is sales-by-customer-expanded-

{range}.csv. {range}

uses this map from range label: Today → today; Yesterday → yesterday; This Week → this_week; Last Week → last_week; This Month → this_month; Last Month → last_month; This Year → this_year; Last Year → last_year; This Quarter → this_quarter; Last Quarter → last_quarter; Custom → custom."

The same specification, requirement S15-R6, applies the same naming to the printable files: "The files follow the same version-and-range naming as the CSV (S14-R14) with a .pdf extension."

renderedFields.description:
What happens now

On the Sales By Customer report the Customer filter works, but three things about how it looks and reads are not what the written description asks for.

One: the control has no magnifier (search) icon on it, so nothing tells the user it can be searched. The only icon on it is the drop-down arrow. The Location filter beside it does carry its own icons, so this is not a general styling choice.

Two: with two customers picked the closed control reads "2 customers". The written description asks for "2 selected".

Three: while the user types a search, the closed control keeps reading "All customers" (or whatever the summary was). The typed text goes into a separate search box inside the open list, and never appears in the control itself.

How to see it

Open Reports, then Sales By Customer. Look at the Customer filter in the toolbar: there is no magnifier icon.

Open the Customer filter and type Aacrest, then tick Aacrest Works. Type Aacastle and tick Aacastle Services. Close the list. The control reads "2 customers".

Open it again and type any text. Watch the closed control behind the list: it still shows the summary label, not what you typed.

What should happen instead

The control should carry a magnifier icon, the two-or-more label should read "2 selected", and while the user is typing, the control should show the typed text in place of the summary label.

What we tested it on

QA branch sv8582, build v3.5-16cf83f, on 6 August 2026. Viewport 1680x1050, desktop Chrome. Test data: customers Aacrest Works and Aacastle Services, date range This Month, Product Type Parts & Service, both locations selected.

How bad is it

Low. The filter itself finds and applies the right customers; only its wording and its icon are wrong. The missing magnifier is the most likely one to matter, because nothing on screen tells a new user the list can be searched.

What we ruled out

We checked that the search itself is correct before raising this: typing matches anywhere inside a name (not only the start), the list is limited to customers with invoices in the chosen date range, and a ticked customer shows a checkmark. All of that is right.

Where this expected behaviour comes from

Where this expected behaviour comes from: the Sales By Customer report specification, version 15, requirement S18-R2, which says: "The filter is a multi-select with server-backed type-ahead. The control carries a search (magnifier) icon marking it as searchable.".

Where this expected behaviour comes from: the Sales By Customer report specification, version 15, requirement S18-R5, which says: "The collapsed filter label reads "All customers" when the filter is in the all-customers state, "None" when the selection is an empty set, the customer's name when exactly one customer is selected, and "N selected" when more than one customer is selected. While the user is typing a search query in the filter, the field shows the query text instead of the summary label.".

That is source type 2: the specification (PRD) in Confluence. The version number given is the Confluence page version, not the version written inside the page.

renderedFields.description:
What happens now

Two things about sorting on the Sales By Customer report do not match the written description.

One: every column heading can be clicked to sort except two - the little arrow column at the far left, which is correct, and the Location column, which is not. Location has no sort arrow and clicking it does nothing. The server itself can sort by location perfectly well, so this is only missing from the screen.

Two: rows with no value in them sort to the wrong end. Sorting Margin % smallest-first puts all the blank ones at the TOP, and largest-first puts them at the BOTTOM. The written description asks for the exact opposite.

How to see it

Open Reports, then Sales By Customer, and choose This Year so there are plenty of rows.

Click each column heading in turn. Every one sorts except Location, which has no arrow and does not respond.

Click Margin % once (smallest first). The first rows shown have a dash instead of a percentage. Click again (largest first) and the dashes have moved to the end.

What should happen instead

Location should sort like every other column. Blank values should go to the bottom when sorting smallest-first and to the top when sorting largest-first.

What we tested it on

QA branch sv8582, build v3.5-16cf83f, on 6 August 2026. Date range This Year (1 January to 6 August 2026), both locations, Product Type Parts & Service, 384 customers in the set. 19 of the first 30 rows had no Margin % value.

How bad is it

Low. Sorting works on the other twelve columns and the order it produces is correct; it is the blank rows that end up in the wrong place, and one column that cannot be sorted at all.

What we ruled out

We checked the sort is genuinely applied and not a stale screen: each click sends a fresh request and the first page comes back in the new order, and the heading itself reports which way it is sorted. We also confirmed the server accepts a sort by location and answers correctly, so the gap is on the screen only.

Where this expected behaviour comes from

Where this expected behaviour comes from: the Sales By Customer report specification, version 15, requirement S10-R1, which says: "Every column is sortable except the chevron column.".

Where this expected behaviour comes from: the Sales By Customer report specification, version 15, requirement S10-R3, which says: "A missing value sorts to the bottom in ascending order and to the top in descending order; a Margin % em-dash cell counts as a missing value.".

That is source type 2: the specification (PRD) in Confluence. The version number given is the Confluence page version, not the version written inside the page.

renderedFields.description:
What happens now

The Sales By Customer report offers two PDF downloads. The Summary one is A4 landscape, which is right. The Expanded View one comes out on A3 landscape - a sheet half again as wide.

Anyone printing it on ordinary office paper will get it shrunk down or cropped.

How to see it

Open Reports, then Sales By Customer. Open the download menu and choose Download Expanded View (PDF).

Open the file and look at its page size. It measures 1190 by 842 points, which is A3. The Summary PDF from the same menu measures 842 by 595 points, which is A4.

What should happen instead

Both PDFs should be A4 landscape.

What we tested it on

QA branch sv8582, build v3.5-16cf83f, on 6 August 2026. Date range 1 to 6 August 2026, Product Type Parts & Service, both locations. Both files downloaded from the report own download menu.

How bad is it

Low. The file opens and every figure in it is correct; it is the paper size that is wrong.

What we ruled out

This is not a one-off: the Summary PDF from the same menu, the same filters and the same moment is correctly A4, so it is specific to the Expanded View file. The footer, the heading block and the logo are all present and correct in both.

Where this expected behaviour comes from

Where this expected behaviour comes from: the Sales By Customer report specification, version 15, requirement S15-R7, which says: "The PDF is A4 landscape with 25px margins on all sides, using the application's standard font.".

The same requirement covers both files: the specification says the header title reads the same for both versions and that only the file name tells them apart (S15-R13), so there is no separate paper size for the Expanded View.

That is source type 2: the specification (PRD) in Confluence. The version number given is the Confluence page version, not the version written inside the page.

renderedFields.description:
What happens now

The Sales By Customer report remembers the filters a user left behind. If one of those remembered choices is no longer a real choice, the report should quietly drop it and fall back to the normal default. Two of the four do not.

A remembered location that no longer exists is kept: the Location filter comes back reading "1 selected" for something the user cannot see or name.

A remembered customer that no longer exists is kept the same way: the Customer filter reads "1 selected".

A remembered date range that is no longer a valid choice is not replaced by the normal default either. The date control comes back reading "Select Date Range" and the report shows no rows at all, so the user is left on an empty report with no obvious reason why.

Product Type and the chosen columns do fall back correctly.

How to see it

Open Reports, then Sales By Customer, so the remembered view is created. Then make the remembered view hold a location id and a customer id that do not exist, and a date range value that is not one of the offered ranges.

Reload the report. The date control reads "Select Date Range", the table is empty, and Location and Customer each read "1 selected". Product Type has gone back to Parts & Service and every column is showing again.

What should happen instead

Anything remembered that is no longer valid should be dropped and the report should fall back to that filter default - This Month for the date range, All locations, and all customers.

What we tested it on

QA branch sv8582, build v3.5-16cf83f, on 6 August 2026. The remembered view is held in the browser under the name report_view:sales-by-customer.

How bad is it

Low. Nothing is lost and the user can put the filters right by hand. The date range one is the least pleasant, because the report looks broken - completely empty - rather than simply filtered.

What we ruled out

We first checked that remembering works at all, and it does: date range, Product Type, locations, sort and the chosen columns are all restored exactly. We also confirmed each report keeps its own separate remembered view, so nothing here spills between reports.

Where this expected behaviour comes from

Where this expected behaviour comes from: the Sales By Customer report specification, version 15, requirement S6-R5, which says: "On restore, any saved value that is no longer valid is discarded, and that setting uses its default instead.".

Where this expected behaviour comes from: the Sales By Customer report specification, version 15, requirement S6-R6, which says: "A saved value is treated as no longer valid when it is an unknown date range, a location the user no longer has access to, a sort column that no longer exists, or a column set that does not match the current columns.".

Where this expected behaviour comes from: the Sales By Customer report specification, version 15, requirement S18-R9, which says: "in a subset selection, a selected customer that is no longer present is dropped from the selection and must be re-selected to appear.".

Note on scope: S6-R6 lists the date range and the location, so those two are squarely covered. The customer half rests on S18-R9 instead, which is the requirement that says a selected customer no longer present is dropped from the selection.

That is source type 2: the specification (PRD) in Confluence. The version number given is the Confluence page version, not the version written inside the page.

renderedFields.description:
What happens now

On the Work In Progress report the WO number in the first column is plain black text. It is not a link, nothing happens when you click it, and there is no way to get from the report to the work order.

This was checked signed in as an administrator who does hold Work Orders access, so it is not the permission rule doing its job - the whole table contains no links at all.

How to see it

Open Reports, then Work In Progress. Click any WO number, for example S8582-16256. Nothing happens and the address bar does not change.

The cell is an ordinary piece of text: no underline, black, and the mouse pointer does not change to a hand over it.

What should happen instead

For a user who has Work Orders access the WO number should be a link that opens that work order in the same tab, so the user can look at the job and come back with the browser back button. A user WITHOUT Work Orders access should see it as plain text - which is what everyone sees today.

What we tested it on

QA branch sv8582, build v3.5-16cf83f, on 6 August 2026. Signed in as Admin ShopView, whose permissions include Work Orders View, Create & Edit and Delete. Date range This Week, both locations, on the Approved - Partially Completed tab.

How bad is it

Low, but it removes the one thing that makes the report actionable: a service manager reading it cannot jump to the job to do anything about it.

What we ruled out

We confirmed the user really does hold Work Orders access before raising this, and we clicked the number rather than only inspecting it. We also checked the rest of the row: every other cell is correct and the report data itself is right.

Where this expected behaviour comes from

Where this expected behaviour comes from: the Work In Progress report specification, version 9, requirement S4-R5, which says: "WO # is shown as a link that opens the work order in the same browser tab (the user returns via the browser's back navigation) only when the user has permission to access Work Orders. A user without Work Order permission sees the WO # as plain text, not a link.".

This requirement was rewritten on 5 August 2026 to spell out both halves - the link for someone with permission, and plain text for someone without. The half that gives the link is the half that is missing.

That is source type 2: the specification (PRD) in Confluence. The version number given is the Confluence page version, not the version written inside the page.

renderedFields.description:
What happens now

The written description asks for the Work In Progress report to load the complete set of open jobs in one request, and then for the Advisor, Customer and Asset filters to narrow what you see on screen without going back to the server.

That is not what happens. Ticking an advisor or a customer sends a fresh request to the server with the choice attached, and the table is rebuilt from the answer. Switching tab afterwards carries those choices to the server too.

How to see it

Open Reports, then Work In Progress. Open the Advisor filter and tick Admin ShopView: a fresh request goes out. Open the Customer filter and tick Aaborough Works: another fresh request goes out.

Now click the Estimates tab. The request that follows carries both choices with it, so the narrowing is being done by the server, not on screen.

What should happen instead

The report should load the open jobs once, and ticking an advisor, a customer or an asset should simply hide the rows that do not match, with no new request.

What we tested it on

QA branch sv8582, build v3.5-16cf83f, on 6 August 2026. Date range This Week, both locations, advisor Admin ShopView, customer Aaborough Works.

How bad is it

Low. The filtering itself gives the right answer - the rows, the Totals row and the summary figures all agree with the choice made. It is how the answer is produced that differs, which matters mainly for speed and for how the report behaves on a slow connection.

What we ruled out

We checked the results are correct before raising this: filtering to one customer left the right jobs on screen, the Totals row recalculated to match, and the summary figures moved with it. We also confirmed the filter lists themselves are drawn from the full scope, which is the other half of the requirement and is right.

Where this expected behaviour comes from

Where this expected behaviour comes from: the Work In Progress report specification, version 9, requirement S7-R1, which says: "The toolbar has an Advisor filter, a multi-select listing the advisors present across all open jobs in the current scope (the report loads the complete set of open jobs in one request). Selecting one or more advisors narrows the visible jobs to those advisors, on screen only (no reload).".

Where this expected behaviour comes from: the Work In Progress report specification, version 9, requirement S7-R2, which says: "The toolbar has a Customer filter ... The user types to narrow the list and selects one or more customers; narrowing is on screen only (no reload).".

Where this expected behaviour comes from: the Work In Progress report specification, version 9, requirement S7-R4, which says: "The toolbar has an Asset filter ... Selecting one or more assets narrows the visible jobs on screen only (no reload).".

These three requirements were rewritten on 5 August 2026, which is why they are worth checking now.

That is source type 2: the specification (PRD) in Confluence. The version number given is the Confluence page version, not the version written inside the page.

renderedFields.description:
What happens now

Two small things about the three Work In Progress filters do not match the written description.

One: each filter offers its Clear action all the time, even before anything has been picked. The description asks for it to appear only once at least one thing is selected. It is also labelled "Clear all" where the description calls it a single "Clear" action.

Two: the Customer and Asset filters each have an "All customers" / "All assets" item pinned at the top of their list, but the Advisor filter has no "All advisors" item at all - its list starts with "Clear all" and then the advisors. The closed control does read "All advisors", so the state exists; it is the item that is missing.

How to see it

Open Reports, then Work In Progress, without touching any filter.

Open the Customer filter: the list reads "All customers", "Clear all", then the customers - and nothing is selected yet. The Asset filter behaves the same way.

Open the Advisor filter: the list reads "Clear all", then Admin ShopView. There is no "All advisors" item.

What should happen instead

The Clear action should appear only once something is selected, and the Advisor filter should offer an "All advisors" item like the other two.

What we tested it on

QA branch sv8582, build v3.5-16cf83f, on 6 August 2026. Date range This Week, both locations, nothing selected in any filter.

How bad is it

Low. Everything still works - Clear all does return the filter to its all state, and the closed control shows the right words. It is only when each control appears that differs.

What we ruled out

We checked the useful half first: each filter does list the values found across the whole scope, the closed labels do read "All advisors", "All customers" and "All assets", and Clear all does put the filter back.

Where this expected behaviour comes from

Where this expected behaviour comes from: the Work In Progress report specification, version 9, requirement S7-R3, which says: "When no customer is selected, the Customer filter reads "All customers" and every job is shown; the filter offers a single "Clear" action that returns it to "All customers", shown only once at least one customer is selected.".

Where this expected behaviour comes from: the Work In Progress report specification, version 9, requirement S7-R5, which says: "When no asset is selected, the Asset filter reads "All assets" and every job is shown; the filter offers a single "Clear" action that returns it to "All assets", shown only once at least one asset is selected.".

The Advisor filter half rests on S7-R1, which describes the Advisor filter as the same kind of multi-select as the other two.

That is source type 2: the specification (PRD) in Confluence. The version number given is the Confluence page version, not the version written inside the page.

What happens now

The written description asks the Work In Progress table to be all white - white column headings and white data cells, with no alternating shading.

Every part of the table is the pale blue-grey instead: the headings, every data row and the Totals row all read as the same off-white tint. There is at least no alternating shading, which is the other half of the requirement.

How to see it

Open Reports, then Work In Progress. The heading row, the data rows and the Totals row all read as rgb(249, 250, 251) rather than white.

What should happen instead

White column headings and white data cells.

What we tested it on

QA branch sv8582, build v3.5-16cf83f, on 6 August 2026, light mode, 1680x1050, on the Approved - Partially Completed tab and again on the Estimates tab.

How bad is it

Low. The table is perfectly readable and every figure in it is correct; it does not match the agreed look.

What we ruled out

We checked the parts of the requirement that are right rather than only the part that is wrong: there is no alternating row shading, the Totals row is bold, and the summary figures above the table each carry a keyboard-reachable information button with a full plain-English explanation.

Where this expected behaviour comes from

Where this expected behaviour comes from: the Work In Progress report specification, version 9, requirement S10-R1, which says: "Each tab uses an all-white table: white column headers and white data cells, with no alternating row shading.".

That is source type 2: the specification (PRD) in Confluence. The version number given is the Confluence page version, not the version written inside the page.

The Sales By Representative report can be downloaded as an "Expanded View" spreadsheet, one line per invoice.

Two things in its heading row are not what the written description asks for. The Invoice # column comes BEFORE the Date column instead of after it, and the status column is headed "Invoice Status" instead of "Status".

renderedFields.description:
1. What happens now

When you expand a representative, the invoices underneath are listed newest first, which is right.

But when several invoices fall on the SAME DAY, they come out in the order they happened to be created rather than by invoice number, so the numbers appear in no order at all.

Read from the report, on 12 June 2026 the rows run: S-15487, P-117, P-113, S-15750, S-15646, S-15828, S-15812.

The same thing happens on a small representative: ZZAUTOTEST RepB has three invoices all dated 04 August 2026 and they come out S-16243, S-16242, S-16241 - counting downwards, where they should count upwards.

2. What should happen instead

Invoices sharing a date should be listed by invoice number counting UPWARDS by the number after the P or S - so on 12 June 2026: P-113, P-117, S-15487, S-15646, S-15750, S-15812, S-15828. Where the day and the number both match, the P (parts) invoice comes before the S (service) one.

3. Branch / environment

Application https://sv8582.qa.shopview.com, API host https://sv8582api.qa.shopview.com.

Build marker (app-version meta tag) v3.5-7168d14, index.html last modified Thu 06 Aug 2026 08:32:37 GMT.

Observed on 2026-08-06. Organisation Staging Foothills Group Inc. Signed in as admin@shopview.com (Admin ShopView).

Test data named in full: sales representatives ZZAUTOTEST RepA (1 invoice, S-16244) and ZZAUTOTEST RepB (3 invoices, S-16243, S-16242, S-16241), plus Parth Fadadu (1 invoice, S-15826). Customers Aaborough Works, Aacastle Services, Aachester Partners, Aacrest Works, Beman Systems. Locations Staging Heavy Duty - 9919 and Staging Lethbridge - 4310.

4. How bad is it

Low. Every figure is correct; it is the order within a single day. It matters most where a day holds many invoices, because there is then no way to find one by its number.

5. What we ruled out

We checked the main sort first and it is correct: across days the report does run newest first - 06 August, then 04 August, 31 July, 12 June, 11 June, 10 June. We proved the same-day problem on a large set (849 invoice lines) as well as a small one, so it is not a quirk of one representative.

6. Where this expected behaviour comes from

Where this expected behaviour comes from: the Sales By Representative report specification, version 17, requirement S6-R9, which says: "invoice detail rows are ordered by invoice date descending (newest first), tie-broken by invoice number ascending by the numeric portion after the P/S prefix (numeric, not lexical - so S999 precedes S1000); if both the date and the numeric portion tie (e.g., P100 and S100 on the same day), P (Parts) sorts before S (Service).". That is source type 2: the specification (PRD) in Confluence. The version number given is the Confluence page version, not the version written inside the page.

1. What happens now

Three of the five icon-only controls give a screen-reader name that is not the one written down.

The three-dot download button announces "Export report" instead of "Report actions".

The column button announces "Column Selection" instead of "Show or hide columns".

The chevron at the top of the table announces "Expand all representatives" and "Collapse all representatives" instead of "Expand all reps" and "Collapse all reps".

2. What should happen instead

Each should announce the name the written description gives it, word for word.

3. Branch / environment

Customers Aaborough Works, Aacastle Services, Aachester Partners, Aacrest Works, Beman Systems. Locations Staging Heavy Duty - 9919 and Staging Lethbridge - 4310.

4. How bad is it

Low. Every control works, and a screen-reader user is told something sensible - just not the agreed wording, so it does not match the rest of the suite.

5. What we ruled out

We checked all five before raising this. The per-row chevrons ARE correct - they announce "Expand ZZAUTOTEST RepA" and change to "Collapse ZZAUTOTEST RepA". We also confirmed the controls are properly keyboard operable, so this is the name only and not the behaviour.

6. Where this expected behaviour comes from

Where this expected behaviour comes from: the Sales By Representative report specification, version 17, requirement S18-R9, which says: "Every icon-only control has an accessible name: exports = "Report actions"; column selector = "Show or hide columns"; per-row chevron = "Expand

{rep name}" / "Collapse {rep name}

"; header chevron = "Expand all reps" / "Collapse all reps"; dialog X = "Close".". That is source type 2: the specification (PRD) in Confluence. The version number given is the Confluence page version, not the version written inside the page.

renderedFields.description:
1. What happens now

The report remembers your filters in the browser. If the saved date range is one the report no longer recognises, it does not fall back to the normal default.

Instead the date button reads "Select Date Range", no data is asked for at all, and the report sits there empty with the no-data message.

The user has no way of telling that anything went wrong - it simply looks as though there is no sales activity.

2. What should happen instead

A saved value that is no longer valid should quietly fall back to that setting default - here, This Month - and the report should load normally.

3. Branch / environment

Application https://sv8582.qa.shopview.com, API host https://sv8582api.qa.shopview.com.

Build marker (app-version meta tag) v3.5-7168d14, index.html last modified Thu 06 Aug 2026 08:32:37 GMT.

Observed on 2026-08-06. Organisation Staging Foothills Group Inc. Signed in as admin@shopview.com (Admin ShopView).

Test data named in full: sales representatives ZZAUTOTEST RepA (1 invoice, S-16244) and ZZAUTOTEST RepB (3 invoices, S-16243, S-16242, S-16241), plus Parth Fadadu (1 invoice, S-15826). Customers Aaborough Works, Aacastle Services, Aachester Partners, Aacrest Works, Beman Systems. Locations Staging Heavy Duty - 9919 and Staging Lethbridge - 4310.

4. How bad is it

Low, but misleading: an empty report reads as "no sales", not as "your saved setting was dropped".

5. What we ruled out

We checked that every OTHER saved setting does fall back correctly: an unknown sort column, an unknown column list, an unknown product type and an unknown invoice status all quietly revert to their defaults and are rewritten in the browser. It is the date range alone that does not. Nothing errors, so the "never causes an error" half of the requirement is met.

6. Where this expected behaviour comes from

Where this expected behaviour comes from: the Sales By Representative report specification, version 17, requirement S23-R3, which says: "Restoration is defensive: a remembered value that is no longer valid (a location the user can no longer access, a range or sort column that no longer exists, a hidden-but-sorted column) falls back to that setting's default rather than being sent to the server.". That is source type 2: the specification (PRD) in Confluence. The version number given is the Confluence page version, not the version written inside the page.

In the Work In Progress report, switch the Last Activity column on in Column Selection. Its heading and its values sit on the LEFT of the column.

Requirement S4-R4 names the columns that are left-aligned and then covers all the rest in one sentence: "WO #, Status, Customer, Asset, VIN, Location, and Advisor are left-aligned; every other column is right-aligned."

renderedFields.description:
What happens now

In the summary strip across the top of the Work In Progress report, the ESTIMATES figure looks exactly like the other figures. Its label and its amount use the same grey label and the same dark value colour as NOT STARTED, STARTED - EARNED, STARTED - REMAINING and READY TO INVOICE, at the same size and the same weight.

Nothing about it is toned down, so a reader cannot tell by looking that it is the one figure that is deliberately left out of the two headline totals.

What should happen instead

Requirement S5-R8 says the Estimates figure "is the total quoted value of the jobs in the 'Estimates' tab, and is shown in a muted style."

It should be visibly quieter than the figures that do count toward the totals.

How to see it

Open Reports, then Work In Progress, and set the date range to Last 12 Months so there are estimates to show. Compare the ESTIMATES figure at the right-hand end of the strip with NOT STARTED or READY TO INVOICE. They are styled identically.

What we tested it on

QA branch sv8582, build v3.5-f77875c, on 6 August 2026. Date range Last 12 Months, both locations (Staging Heavy Duty - 9919 and Staging Lethbridge - 4310). The Estimates figure read $527,356.34 alongside NOT STARTED $31,172.38 and READY TO INVOICE $56,494.23.

How bad is it

Low. The amount itself is correct - it matches the Estimates tab's own total exactly - and it is correctly left out of Total Earned and Total Remaining. Only the styling differs.

Where this expectation comes from

The Work In Progress report specification on Confluence, version 9 - the numbered requirement is named in each section below. The owning story is the parent of this ticket, and that story sits under epic SV-8582 Open .

renderedFields.description:
What happens now

Switch the Inv. Hrs column on in the Work In Progress report. Every value carries TWO decimal places - for example +0.50, +1.24, -0.81, -14.86 - and a zero reads 0.00.

The Totals row at the foot of each tab does the same: +246.84, +1434.65, +0.52, +173.50.

What should happen instead

Requirement S4-R23 asks for "a signed number with one decimal place (\"+2.0\", \"-14.0\", \"0.0\"). A zero value shows unsigned as \"0.0\" (never \"+0.0\" or blank)."

So the same values should read +0.5, +1.2, -0.8, -14.9 and 0.0.

How to see it

Open Reports, then Work In Progress. Set the date range to Last 12 Months. Open Column Selection and switch Inv. Hrs on. Read any value in that column, and the Totals row at the bottom.

What we tested it on

QA branch sv8582, build v3.5-f77875c, on 6 August 2026. Date range Last 12 Months, both locations (Staging Heavy Duty - 9919 and Staging Lethbridge - 4310). Checked on all four tabs.

How bad is it

Low. The sign is right, the zero is correctly unsigned, and the arithmetic is right - it is the number of decimal places that differs. The green and red colouring of the values is also correct.

Where this expectation comes from

The Work In Progress report specification on Confluence, version 9 - the numbered requirement is named in each section below. The owning story is the parent of this ticket, and that story sits under epic SV-8582 Open .
